verdict.rationale: Letta keeps one persistent agent and its memory reachable across its own interfaces and Slack (letta-docs-17, letta-docs-24, letta-docs-52), and shared memory lets multiple Letta agents use the same context (letta-docs-21). Third-party clients can drive a Letta agent through the App Server's OpenAI-compatible API (e.g., Open WebUI) or the ACP adapter (e.g., Zed) (letta-docs-23, letta-docs-93), but that routes them to Letta's agent rather than letting Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor read and write a shared memory store. The only memory-exposing bridge is a community-built MCP server (letta-comm-2), and the cross-tool portability claim covers skills, not memory (letta-docs-57). Missing for 10: an official way to connect Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor to Letta memory (e.g., a first-party MCP server), documented setup for those specific tools, and hands-on evidence of cross-tool memory sharing.
